lesson.title: Doing Things Together
lesson.subtitle: Inviting someone to lunch and deciding where to go
lesson.description: Learn to invite someone for lunch, accept or decline, and agree on a place to eat.

learning_objectives: Invite another person to eat or drink with you.
Ask who someone is going with.

blocks.text: Learn to invite someone for lunch, accept or decline, and agree on a place to eat. Use the model conversation to notice the expressions, then practice the patterns and speak aloud.

turns.speaker: A
turns.hanzi: 你想跟我一起吃午饭吗？
turns.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma?
turns.english: Would you like to have lunch with me?

turns.speaker: B
turns.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ yě xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī.
turns.english: Yes, I would like to eat with you too.

turns.speaker: B
turns.english: Let us go to a restaurant.

blocks.pattern_hanzi: 跟 + 人 + 一起 + 动作
blocks.function_en: 跟 (gēn) introduces the person accompanying you; 一起 (yìqǐ) means together.

example.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chīfàn.
example.english: I would like to eat with you.
example.teaching_note: Use this when inviting someone to share a meal or activity.

blocks.pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 也 + 想 + 动作
blocks.function_en: 也 (yě) adds agreement or another participant doing the same thing.

example.teaching_note: A friendly response when you want to join someone else’s plan.

items.hanzi: 你想跟我一起吃午饭吗
items.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma
items.meaning_en: Would you like to have lunch with me?

items.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn
items.meaning_en: I would like to have lunch with you.

items.hanzi: 我也想跟你一起吃午饭
items.pinyin: wǒ yě xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn
items.meaning_en: I would also like to have lunch with you.

items.hanzi: 你想跟我一起吃晚饭吗
items.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn ma
items.meaning_en: Would you like to have dinner with me?

items.pinyin: wǒ bù xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ hē
items.meaning_en: I do not want to drink with you.
items.usage_note: The object of 喝 (hē) is understood if the speakers already know what drink is being discussed. Without that context, the refusal sounds abrupt or incomplete. A softer, more explicit alternative is 我今天不太想跟你一起喝茶 (wǒ jīntiān bú tài xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ hē chá).

items.hanzi: 你想跟我一起喝一点东西吗
items.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ hē yìdiǎn dōngxi ma
items.meaning_en: Would you like to have a drink with me?

items.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn
items.meaning_en: I would like to have dinner with you.

items.pinyin: nǐ bù xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ hē
items.meaning_en: You do not want to drink with me.
items.usage_note: The drink after 喝 (hē) is omitted because it is understood from the conversation. As an isolated sentence this can sound abrupt. A more explicit form is 你不想跟我一起喝茶 (nǐ bù xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ hē chá).

items.hanzi: 我想跟你一起喝一点东西
items.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ hē yìdiǎn dōngxi
items.meaning_en: I would like to have a drink with you.

blocks.text: Speaking task: Invite someone to lunch, accept or decline, and decide where to go together.

questions.prompt: Does speaker B accept the lunch invitation?
questions.answer: 好，我也想跟你一起吃。 (Hǎo, wǒ yě xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī.) — Yes, I would like to eat with you too.
questions.explanation: Check the model dialogue and identify the relevant response.

questions.prompt: Translate into Mandarin: Would you like to have lunch with me?
questions.answer: 你想跟我一起吃午饭吗 (nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma)
questions.explanation: One model answer; another natural equivalent may be acceptable.

questions.prompt: Say that you also want to go, using 也 (yě).
questions.answer: 我也想去。 (Wǒ yě xiǎng qù.) — I want to go too.
questions.explanation: One natural model response; alternatives that express the same meaning are possible.

questions.prompt: Invite someone to lunch, accept or decline, and decide where to go together.
questions.answer:
A: 你想跟我一起吃午饭吗？ (Nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒ yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma?) — Would you like to have lunch with me?
B: 好，我想跟你一起吃。 (Hǎo, wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ yìqǐ chī.) — Yes, I would like to eat with you.
A: 我们去哪儿吃？ (Wǒmen qù nǎr chī?) — Where shall we eat?
B: 我们去饭店吧。 (Wǒmen qù fàndiàn ba.) — Let us go to a restaurant.
questions.explanation: Complete sample role-play. practice both speakers, then substitute your own details.
